data.narrative:
Nabla Bio is a Series A-stage biotech company founded by Surge Biswas and Frances Anastassacos, operating within a sector populated by 3 public comparables (RXRX, TEM, ONT.L) and 8 private peers including Colossal Biosciences, Chai Discovery, and Recursion Pharmaceuticals. The company has raised $37M plus $1.5B+ in partnerships to date.

The analysis applies stage-progression methodology as the primary valuation anchor. Using the $37M total raised as a proxy for post-money Series A valuation and applying a 2.0x step-up multiplier typical for progression to the next financing stage yields an implied valuation of $74M. Peer-median triangulation is inapplicable due to insufficient same-stage or adjacent-stage comparables within the narrow biotech peer set; while 7 same-sector peers exist, none of the filtered subsets met the minimum three-datapoint threshold. Public-comp anchoring via P/S multiples is not feasible absent disclosed target revenue, though the sector median P/S of 6.2x across the three public biotech tickers provides context for future calibration if revenue becomes available.

The triangulated valuation range of $63M–$85M (median $74M) reflects conservative and optimistic variants around the single applicable method. Key uncertainties include the revenue profile and capital efficiency trajectory relative to peer benchmarks, partnership value realization, and stage-specific risk adjustment factors. This range should be stress-tested as additional financial disclosure becomes available.
